crit: 15 imbalanced datasets (eleven real, four artificial) 'that were commonly used in the related studies (Janicka et al., 2019; Lango & Stefanowski, 2018)'; 'The selected datasets are diversified, including problems with multi-majority, multi-minority, and gradual class size configurations; with different levels of class overlapping and with different numbers of classes', IR from 2 to 164.
benchmark_inherited_from: Janicka et al., 2019 (SOUP) and Lango & Stefanowski, 2018: datasets 'commonly used in the related studies'; minority/majority class assignment 'taken from the previous paper on SOUP (Janicka et al., 2019)'
notes: Table 1 (p.5194) prints only class names and class cardinalities (minority vs majority); no n_instances, n_features or per-dataset IR. Merged classes are visible only through labels in Table 1 (Cleveland_2 '0+1', Vehicle 'opel_saab', Ecoli 'imUimS', 'omomL', 'cpimL'); the paper never says who merged them (possibly inherited from Janicka et al., 2019). Released-data link covers only the original UCI data and the artificial sets (multi-imbalance repository), not the merged versions; online appendix (footnote 3) holds results. The 4 artificial datasets (Art1-Art4: MIN1 120, MIN2 240, MAJ 840) are taken ready-made from the multi-imbalance repository; the authors do not generate them or describe a generator, so 'Generated' not coded (source still Synthetic). Contraceptive: majority class 1 printed as 333, the same as minority class 2 (333); possible typo. Wine quality lists classes 5, 6, 7, 8 only (199/81/681/638), with no explanation of other classes. IR defined p.5185 as biggest class size / smallest class size.
